title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths
population: 20 healthy adults trained one leg seated and the other prone; 12 untrained controls joined the muscle-damage part.
key_findings: Seated leg curls, which train the hamstrings at longer muscle lengths, grew the whole hamstrings more than prone leg curls over 12 weeks (+14% versus +9% muscle volume).
The difference showed in the biarticular hamstring muscles, not in the monoarticular one.
Both conditions protected similarly against damage from later eccentric exercise.
methods: Within-participant comparison (one leg each condition): 5 sets of 10 at 70% of 1RM, twice a week for 12 weeks, with MRI muscle volume; then an eccentric bout with MRI T2 and 1RM over 72 hours.
limitations: One pair of exercises and one muscle group; the abstract does not report randomization of legs or the training status of participants.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
